CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right finger pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sharon Brooks is a 48-year-old female presenting with right index finger pain. Patient reports she was skiing over the weekend and attempted moguls. While coming down the hill, her strap caught on her finger and bent it backward. The incident occurred on Sunday, approximately 4 days prior to presentation. Patient has tried ice and ibuprofen for pain management with some relief, but pain persists. Pain is worse with movement. No other associated symptoms reported.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Otherwise unremarkable except as noted in HPI.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Constipation (recent)
Appendectomy at age 18

MEDICATIONS
Miralax
Ibuprofen as needed

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Participates in skiing

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right index finger: Tenderness over distal phalanx and distal interphalangeal joint. No tenderness over proximal interphalangeal joint or metacarpophalangeal joint. Full range of motion with ability to flex, extend, and touch thumb to finger. Pain elicited with flexion.

RESULTS
X-ray right index finger: No fractures noted. Normal alignment throughout.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right hand index finger contusion at the distal phalanx. Recommend aluminum foam splint for immobilization. Motrin 600 mg every 6 hours for approximately 1 week. Patient instructed to follow up if symptoms do not improve.
